title: IN PHOTOS | TIFF movies and moments
summary: See highlights from the Toronto International Film Festival, featuring nearly 300 titles, 800 guests and thousands of industry delegates during the 11-day event that started on Thursday.

image.caption: During the Toronto International Film Festival, CBC News will feature highlights from red carpet premieres, fan excitement and other festival moments. (Carlos Osorio/Reuters, Rodin Eckenroth/Getty Images, Brian de Rivera Simon/Getty Images, Sonia Recchia/Getty Images)

blocks.text: Film fans and stars are flocking to Canada's largest city for the Toronto International Film Festival. The 51st edition of TIFF, which runs for 11 days (September 10-20), features nearly 300 titles and big-name actors, including Javier Bardem, Cynthia Erivo and Seth Rogen, among others.
Each day, we will feature highlights from red carpet premieres, fan excitement and other festival moments, so keep scrolling.

items: TIFF's at a turning point — but how will the film festival's new focus on dealmaking affect fans?

blocks.text: Day 4: Sept. 13

Léa Seydoux (first photo) and Lily-Rose Depp (second photo) attend the premiere of their film, Alpha Gang, which is about aliens that come to Earth to conquer it, and find that the human world has a plague they weren’t ready for.
(Evan Mitsui/CBC)
Cynthia Erivo poses with fans at the premiere of Prima Facie at Roy Thomson Hall. In the film, she plays a British defence lawyer, who primarily defends those accused of sex crimes.
(Sonia Recchia/Getty Images)
Annie Murphy poses on the red carpet at the premiere of her rom-com, All That She Wants. Murphy stars as a millennial, who hooks up with a Gen Zer.
(Brian de Rivera Simon/Getty Images)
Margaret Qualley promotes her film, Love Of Your Life, at the Royal Alexandra Theatre.
(Mark Blinch/Reuters)
Amanda Seyfried attends the premiere of the American prison drama thriller, The Life and Deaths of Wilson Shedd.
(Robin Marchant/Getty Images)
From left to right, director Yeon Sang-ho, and stars Kim Hyun-joo and Bae Hyun-sung pose with fans on Toronto's King Street West at the premiere of Paradise Lost.
(Arturo Holmes/Getty Images)
Julianne Moore greets fans during the premiere of The Debut at the Princess of Wales Theatre.
(Rodin Eckenroth/Getty Images)
Javier Bardem attends the red carpet for The Beloved, in which he stars as an acclaimed film director who casts his estranged daughter, played by Victoria Luengo, second photo, in a period piece.
(Carlos Osorio/Reuters)

Channing Tatum, left, and Gemma Chan promote their film, Josephine, at the Royal Alexandra Theatre. They play the parents of a young girl, played by Mason Reeves, second photo, who are helping their daughter cope after she witnesses a crime.
(Leon Bennett/Getty Images)
Day 3: Sept. 12
Zaria arrives on the red carpet at Roy Thomson Hall to promote the film Misty Green, which was written, directed and produced by Chris Rock, second photo, who also appears in the film.
Lauren Miller Rogen looks at her husband, Seth Rogen, as they promote Babies, a film she wrote and directed.
Seth Rogen and Anna Kendrick, seen below, star in the film about a couple deciding whether they want to be parents.
Sarah Paulson poses ahead of the premiere of her film Closing Night at the Princess of Wales Theatre.

Courtney Cox, centre, directs Evil Genius, which dramatizes a bizarre 2003 bank heist by a pizza delivery man dubbed the "pizza bomber." Patricia Arquette, left, and David Harbour star in the film, which premiered at Roy Thomson Hall.
(Frazer Harrison/Getty Images)
Day 2: Sept. 11
Fans of K-pop superstar Lisa caught a glimpse of her at the premiere of her documentary Always Lalisa at Roy Thomson Hall.
The cast and crew of The Stunt Driver pose on the red carpet at the film's premiere. The film stars Jay Baruchel, in the centre, pointing, and Ed Helms, to his left.
Director Michael Dowse, to Baruchel's right, says he knew Baruchel was perfect for the role of Canadian daredevil Ken Carter after watching him in the film Blackberry.
Baruchel with his wife Rebecca-Jo Dunham-Baruchel.

Rebel Wilson, left, with her wife, Ramona Agruma-Wilson, promotes Girl Group, a film she wrote, directed and starred in alongside Jennifer Coolidge and Randall Park, in second photo, at Roy Thomson Hall.
Actor James McAvoy signs autographs ahead of the premiere of his supernatural drama Faith at the Royal Alexandra Theatre.
Faith co-star Smylie Bradwell, right, who plays the son of a single mom, attends the premiere.
Earlier Friday at Roy Thomson Hall, director Adrian Buitenhuis arrives to promote the film Man in Motion: The Rick Hansen Story.
(Chris Young/The Canadian Press)
Hansen arrives on the red carpet.
Day 1: Sept. 10
Workers roll out the red carpet ahead of Thursday's opening film Being Heumann by Oscar-winning director Siân Heder, as well as the Canadian premieres for Fjord, The Housewife and Stuffed.
Furry friends and visitors pose for photos in front of the TIFF sign on King Street W.
(Carlos Osorio/Reuters, Joel C Ryan/Invision/The Associated Press)
At Roy Thomson Hall, the cast and crew of Being Heumann pose on the red carpet ahead of its premiere.
Actor Rio Finnegan attends the film's premiere.
(Matt Winkelmeyer/Getty Images)
Actor Fan Bingbing, who is a TIFF 2026 Tribute Award honouree, attends the film's premiere.
Toronto Mayor Olivia Chow also attends the premiere.
At the Royal Alexandra Theatre, actor Jodie Comer of Killing Eve fame attends the premiere of Stuffed.
(Cindy Ord/Getty Images)
And the film's director and co-writer Theo Rhys meets fans at the premiere.
Later at the Royal Alexandra Theatre, actor Naomi Watts greets fans as she attends the red carpet for her film The Housewife, directed by Canaadian filmmaker Ben Shirinian.
The Housewife is a historical drama based on a true story that focuses on a couple played by Watts and Luke Evans, also at the premiere.
(Joel C Ryan/Invision/The Associated Press)
